T-1936 sign-off, 2026-11-02: within tolerance under T-3153's rule (a gap two camera fits disagree about), the ruling the house's own records already carry for this same flank (doane_house_1827_prairie: chicagology_doane_exterior.match.json and glessner_blog_print.match.json, 'the south flank past the tower', T-3191). Measured through this camera: the coach house lands where the print shows it (r2's west face renders at x 485-573 px, the carriage opening 521-556 against the print's 522-557, its top about 89 px over its foot against the print's 86-90), while the house's rear corners land at x 627 (the main block's, u 0, v 15.5 in the house's frame) and 658 (the 1911 sheet's south rear step, v 17.1) against the print's close at about x 510, and the flank's stack tops 40-60 px higher than the print's. The eye's sight line to the print's carriage opening passes the step's front cheek (u 14.6) at v 17.6, about 0.5 m clear of it, and then enters the main block's south wall at u 10.1: through this camera no house the sheet draws (24.4 m deep, its rear part 1.6 m out on the south) leaves that opening in view, and the camera that would (the eye further off on a longer lens, T-3191's fit forced onto the rear corner) misses the front T-3171 and T-3176 read. So the disagreement is between the front's camera and the flank's depth, not something this view can lay on either building; the flank's depth stays with the house's own ticket (T-1896) should another picture of it turn up.
